## Summary

- Add explicit `/config` and `/configure` routing with stricter default access for repository variable changes.
- Add `agent-config.yml`, `agent-config.md`, and `apply-repo-config` validation/application helpers for allowlisted Sepo repo variables.
- Update docs and regression tests for config routing, access policy, dry-run validation, and Actions variable apply behavior.

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: b37c622f0e2676a1f8ee90a507c1486fd0042f29 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #321 adds a natural-language repo configuration route for Sepo, closing #316 as part of the broader #314 small-fixes orchestration.
- The intended shape is a GitHub Actions page workflow plus explicit `/config` and `/configure` mention routing.
- The design has the right trust boundary: the agent emits a structured JSON plan, and deterministic code validates and applies repository Actions variable changes.
- The implementation also adds stricter route access, docs, workflow wiring, and tests, but two mutation-safety gaps remain.

## Review
The architecture and rubric fit are strong, but the current PR should not ship until the deterministic apply path is safer. Claude and rubrics reviews were broadly positive; the Codex blocking findings are supported by the current PR head and are concrete enough for automated follow-up.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Config values lack per-variable validation | BLOCKING | [`repo-config.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/b37c622f0e2676a1f8ee90a507c1486fd0042f29/.agent/src/repo-config.ts#L99) accepts any non-empty string/boolean/number for every allowlisted variable. Malformed JSON, enum, boolean, or policy values can be persisted and break later Sepo workflows. |
| Partial apply failures can report no changes | BLOCKING | [`apply-repo-config.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/b37c622f0e2676a1f8ee90a507c1486fd0042f29/.agent/src/cli/apply-repo-config.ts#L52) applies operations sequentially, then the catch path always reports that no variables changed. A later failure can therefore hide earlier successful mutations. |
| Prompt/code allowlist sync is unguarded | WARNING | The prompt, docs, and code allowlist are currently synchronized, but tests only compare code with docs. Future drift could make the model unable to plan variables that the CLI accepts. |
| Dispatch denial summary guard lacks regression coverage | WARNING | The empty-allowlist denial summary fix is valid, but it changes global dispatch-policy messaging without a regression test for ordinary denied-route summaries. |

## Progress
- Confirmed PR #321 targets the natural-language config route requested in #316 and is part of the #314 stacked small-fixes sequence.
- Rubrics review passed, including trusted runtime checkout, delegated authorization, structured plan validation, docs sync, and surgical scope.
- Posted inline comments on `.agent/src/repo-config.ts:99` and `.agent/src/cli/apply-repo-config.ts:52`.
- No existing inline comments or review threads needed resolution or minimization.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Config values lack per-variable validation</summary>

**Cause:** `normalizeVariableValue` only checks generic type, emptiness, NUL, and length, while the allowlist includes variables with stricter runtime contracts such as `AGENT_RUNS_ON`, JSON policy variables, booleans, and provider/session enums.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a per-variable validator map and reuse existing typed parsers where available. At minimum, validate JSON policies, runner JSON, booleans, numeric limits, and enum-like settings before any mutation, or narrow the first-pass allowlist to safely validated variables.

**Comments:** This is the main reviewer disagreement: the design reviews considered name allowlisting enough, but the current diff shows the deterministic safety boundary does not validate the values it can write.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Partial apply failures can report no changes</summary>

**Cause:** `applyRepoConfigPlan` is non-transactional and can mutate earlier variables before a later operation throws. The CLI catch path then discards partial state and formats every error as “No repository variables were changed.”

**Candidate solutions:** Apply in an explicit loop that accumulates results, throw a typed partial-apply error containing completed operations and the failed operation, and render a failure summary that distinguishes applied, skipped, and failed rows. Add a fake-`gh` regression test where operation 1 succeeds and operation 2 fails.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Prompt/code allowlist sync is unguarded</summary>

**Cause:** `.github/prompts/agent-config.md` duplicates the variable list, but the current sync test only compares `DEFAULT_REPO_CONFIG_VARIABLES` with `configuration-list.md`.

**Candidate solutions:** Extend the allowlist sync test to extract `AGENT_*` names from the prompt and compare them with both docs and code.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Dispatch denial summary guard lacks regression coverage</summary>

**Cause:** `applyDispatchPolicy` now handles empty allowed lists for config/global-policy intersections, but no test locks the pre-existing denied-route message for standard non-empty allowlists.

**Candidate solutions:** Add one config empty-intersection assertion and one ordinary denied-route assertion so future access-policy changes do not regress either message.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR

Two blocking implementation issues require concrete code and test changes, and the scope is suitable for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Add per-variable validation, or narrow the config-route allowlist, so every settable variable is validated before mutation.
- [ ] Track and report partial apply results when a later repository-variable operation fails after earlier operations already changed state.

@sepo-agent /answer I don't like it. It feels too big... but is it for security concerns?

Yes, mostly security and mutation-safety concerns, but also because this PR implements two entry points at once: the Actions page workflow plus direct `/config` mentions.

The risky part is that this route can change repo Actions variables, including access policy, self-approval, runners, provider, and scheduling. That is why it adds:
- stricter route access: `/config` defaults to `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR`, not `CONTRIBUTOR` ([access-policy.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/30b8d44570ee0ee5b3ae05328b581bf88af53327/.agent/src/access-policy.ts#L28)).
- a scoped prompt that excludes secrets, org/env variables, repo settings, branch protection, and multi-repo writes ([agent-config.md](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/30b8d44570ee0ee5b3ae05328b581bf88af53327/.github/prompts/agent-config.md#L9)).
- model only produces JSON; deterministic code validates/applies it ([agent-config.yml](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/30b8d44570ee0ee5b3ae05328b581bf88af53327/.github/workflows/agent-config.yml#L146), [apply-repo-config.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/30b8d44570ee0ee5b3ae05328b581bf88af53327/.agent/src/cli/apply-repo-config.ts#L47)).
- per-variable validation for booleans, enums, JSON policies, refs, runner labels, etc. ([repo-config.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/30b8d44570ee0ee5b3ae05328b581bf88af53327/.agent/src/repo-config.ts#L243)).
- partial failure reporting so it does not claim “nothing changed” after an earlier mutation succeeded ([repo-config.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/30b8d44570ee0ee5b3ae05328b581bf88af53327/.agent/src/repo-config.ts#L486)).

So I would not remove the deterministic validation/apply layer. That is the part that makes natural-language repo mutation acceptable.

If it feels too big for first ship, the cleanest reduction is product scope, not safety scope: ship only `Agent / Repo Config` from the Actions page first, default dry-run/apply there, and defer direct `/config` mention routing in [agent-router.yml](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/30b8d44570ee0ee5b3ae05328b581bf88af53327/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L728). That would keep the security boundary while reducing the user-facing surface.
